GTA 6: 13 YEARS OF WAITING FOR THIS? IS THE FRANCHISE LOSING ITS IDENTITY?
GTA 6 had one mission: surpass GTA V and deliver an evolution worthy of more than a decade of waiting. After all, we're talking about approximately 13 years between the franchise's two main installments. But did Rockstar really make the most of all that time to deliver what players were expecting?
1. 13 YEARS OF DEVELOPMENT AND STILL 30 FPS? This is undoubtedly one of the most frustrating aspects. After 13 years, an entire generation of technological advancements, and one of the biggest investments in video game history, GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on ****'s hard not to question this decision. We're talking about a franchise that generates billions, a company that had more than a decade to develop its next major release, and a game that promises to revolutionize open-world gaming.Beautiful graphics aren't everything. Smooth performance matters too. In a game involving car chases, shootouts, driving, and constant movement, 60 FPS would make a huge difference. The bare minimum expectation should have been a 60 FPS performance mode, even if it meant sacrificing some graphical quality.After waiting this long, it's frustrating to see that the priority seems to have been visual spectacle rather than delivering the best possible experience in every aspect.
2. IS GTA LOSING ITS IDENTITY? GTA has always been known for its freedom, dark humor, exaggerated violence, and ability to satirize absolutely everything. Politicians, celebrities, corporations, religions, social movements, and American society itself have never been off-limits to Rockstar's jokes.That irreverence was precisely one of the things that made GTA different from every other game.However, there's a growing feeling that Rockstar is adopting a more cautious approach, seemingly concerned with not offending certain **** problem isn't modernizing the franchise. It's changing the very things that made it so popular. GTA was never supposed to be politically correct. Its appeal came from being exaggerated, provocative, and sometimes downright **** Rockstar starts limiting its own creativity to avoid controversy, we're looking at a significant shift in the franchise's identity.
3. LESS FREEDOM FOR THE PLAYER? Perhaps this is the most contradictory aspect of GTA **** decades, GTA built its identity around giving players freedom. You could cause chaos, commit crimes, engage in police chases, and experience absurd situations in an open world.That's why reports of restrictions on certain interactions involving protest characters and specific establishments have sparked so much **** GTA is a franchise about crime, violence, and freedom in an open world, why should certain situations have different limitations? This doesn't mean everything must be allowed in a video game, but it's perfectly reasonable to question the consistency of these decisions. Players shouldn't feel like they're being guided by a list of moral restrictions while exploring a game whose entire premise has always been freedom.Rockstar needs to provide a clearer explanation of this creative direction. After all, selective freedom is still a contradiction for a franchise that has always sold freedom as one of its biggest selling points.
4. THE EXPECTATIONS AFTER 13 YEARS Thirteen years have created enormous expectations. GTA V spanned multiple console generations, while GTA Online continued to be commercially exploited throughout that entire period.That's why GTA 6 needed to deliver much more than impressive graphics. It needed to bring significant improvements to physics, artificial intelligence, missions, player freedom, and the overall **** longer the wait, the greater Rockstar's responsibility to deliver something truly special.
FINAL VERDICT GTA 6 may be visually impressive, technically ambitious, and feature an incredibly detailed world. But that doesn't mean every decision Rockstar has made is the right one.After 13 years, targeting 30 FPS on consoles is disappointing. The potential shift in the franchise's identity and the questions surrounding restrictions on player freedom are also **** biggest fear isn't that GTA 6 will be different. It's that it might abandon the very characteristics that made GTA what it is.Rockstar built one of the greatest franchises in gaming history by being irreverent, provocative, and unafraid to satirize absolutely anything. It shouldn't have to abandon that personality just to follow cultural ****, did we really wait 13 years for a true evolution of GTA, or are we getting a prettier, more restricted, and less irreverent version of what we already knew?
